A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this paper deals with a compressible two-phase flow model with a pressure-dependent well-reservoir interaction.
the model is well-posed and the well-regulation mechanism is stable and robust with respect to the well-formation interaction parameters.

we have shown that a two-phase model with pressure-dependent well- formation interaction is well posed and that there does not exists any time where the gas phase disappears along the well, i.e., that gas will never escape from the well to the formation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we show that a pressure-dependent interaction between the well and the surrounding formation is essential for the well to regulate the flow of gas and liquid.

the pressure-dependent well-reservoir interaction term has a strong stabilizing effect on the system, and that the system is able to regulate itself in a way that the gas is always present in the well.
the model we present here can be used to describe the flow in a well when the surrounding formation is a compressible fluid (gas or liquid) with a pressure dependent well-reservoir interaction.
